headline: Oct 29: HSC and equivalent results to be published
summary: The Inter-Education Board Coordination Committee has announced the date for this year's Higher Secondary Certificate results.
details: The results of this year’s Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations will be published on October 29.
The announcement was made by Prof Syed Akhtaruzzaman, chairman of the Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education, Dhaka.
The decision was reached on Saturday following a meeting with the education minister and the secretary of the education ministry.
Further details regarding the result publication process will be announced on October 26.

headline_marked: 22,000 passengers stranded as [[144 flights to Saudi Arabia cancelled]]
headline: 22,000 passengers stranded as 144 flights to Saudi Arabia cancelled
summary: Flight restrictions at Saudi airports due to Houthi attacks have disrupted both direct and transit routes, affecting thousands of travelers.
details: Restrictions on flight operations at various Saudi Arabian airports have disrupted 144 flights on direct and transit routes to Bangladesh, according to the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB).
A total of 22,021 passengers have been affected by the cancellations and suspensions. The disruption includes 67 direct flights and 77 transit flights.
Direct flight disruptions include 28 flights from Biman Bangladesh Airlines, 10 from US-Bangla Airlines, 19 from Saudia, and 10 from Riyadh Air.
Transit flight disruptions involve 30 flights from IndiGo, 14 from Emirates, 9 from Qatar Airways, 8 from FlyDubai, 7 from Salam Air, 8 from Air India, and 1 flight from Egypt Air.
The restrictions were imposed following attacks by Iran-backed Houthi rebels on Saudi airports, causing widespread disruption to both direct and transit routes.
Biman Bangladesh Airlines announced that flights to Dammam up to October 25 and all flights to Riyadh up to October 31 have been suspended.
However, Biman has confirmed that flights to Jeddah and Medina are operating according to their scheduled time.
Passengers traveling to Riyadh and Dammam may use Jeddah and Medina airports as alternatives, subject to seat availability for emergency needs.
caption:
Over 22,000 passengers are stranded after 144 flights to and from Saudi Arabia were cancelled or suspended.

Restrictions on flight operations at various Saudi Arabian airports have disrupted 144 flights on direct and transit routes to Bangladesh, according to the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB).

A total of 22,021 passengers have been affected by the cancellations and suspensions. The disruption includes 67 direct flights and 77 transit flights.

Direct flight disruptions include 28 flights from Biman Bangladesh Airlines, 10 from US-Bangla Airlines, 19 from Saudia, and 10 from Riyadh Air.

Transit flight disruptions involve 30 flights from IndiGo, 14 from Emirates, 9 from Qatar Airways, 8 from FlyDubai, 7 from Salam Air, 8 from Air India, and 1 flight from Egypt Air.

The restrictions were imposed following attacks by Iran-backed Houthi rebels on Saudi airports, causing widespread disruption to both direct and transit routes.

Biman Bangladesh Airlines announced that flights to Dammam up to October 25 and all flights to Riyadh up to October 31 have been suspended.

However, Biman has confirmed that flights to Jeddah and Medina are operating according to their scheduled time.

Passengers traveling to Riyadh and Dammam may use Jeddah and Medina airports as alternatives, subject to seat availability for emergency needs.

Source: Prothom Alo, Dhaka Tribune
